thread:
ana_support: FYI — Zenith Health wire for $52,400 (INV-2026-0310) was returned by our bank this morning. Customer says they sent on 2026-03-10. Bank return note: invalid IBAN / SWIFT mismatch. Origin ref: ZH-20260310-8873.

ana_support: paste of bank return (from ops):
```
Return reason: INVALID_ACCOUNT_INFORMATION
Corr bank note: Beneficiary account number/IBAN not found
Receiving bank SWIFT: ABOZUS33 -> response: 'Beneficiary not known'
MT103 ref: 2026-03-10 14:12 UTC / Payment amount: 52400.00 USD
```

tom_custliaison: Ugh. I texted the customer — they insist they used the IBAN on the invoice PDF. Can we confirm which IBAN we published for Zenith?

jun_finance: Pulling ledger now. Do we want to automatically re-issue invoice or wait for customer to re-send? We should avoid double-credit.

payments_bot: Ledger note created: internal_payment_id=pay_0G7aK2ZH, external_ref=ZH-20260310-8873, status=returned, amount=52400.00, currency=USD.

lydia_bankops: I'll open a trace with our correspondent bank. Need the customer's sending-bank MT103 copy (proof of payment) or an SWIFT MT103 image to escalate. Without MT103, trace is slow.

ana_support: @tom_custliaison can you ask the customer for: exact wire confirmation screenshot, full MT103/transaction receipt, the sending bank name, sending-bank reference, and the full fields they entered (beneficiary name, IBAN, BIC). Also ask if they used any intermediary bank.

tom_custliaison: On it. Quick checklist I sent them: 
- Screenshot of the wire confirmation (shows IBAN/BIC used)
- Sending bank reference / trace id (MT103)
- Time of transfer + timezone
- Copy of the invoice they paid against

jun_finance: In parallel: mark the invoice payment as "returned - investigation" and do not auto-cancel. I'll put a temporary credit hold so we don't re-invoice or apply late fees until cleared. Also recommend waiving any inbound bank fees if we confirm they used our instructions but bank misrouted.

max_devops: Question for product/UX: we currently accept free-form IBAN text on the billing page. Can we add an IBAN validity check (country & checksum) to catch obvious typos? Not a fix for SWIFT mismatches but reduces bad inputs.

lydia_bankops: Bank trace timeline FYI: once we submit trace with MT103, correspondent bank typically responds 24-72 hours with status (return or reimbursement). If they confirm wrong beneficiary details, funds typically return to sender within 3-5 business days depending on banks.

ana_support: If customer resends, instruct them to include our exact beneficiary name ("Redwood Inference, Inc."), IBAN: GB33BUKB20201555555555 (example) and BIC: BUKBGB22XXX — but do NOT paste live creds until finance confirms. We'll validate before telling them to retry.

tom_custliaison: Customer just replied: they attached a wire confirmation PDF. It shows IBAN ended in 4444, our invoice PDF had IBAN ending 5555. Looks like they transposed the last digit. They say bank told them they keyed it in from the PDF.

jun_finance: OK that's actionable — user error (typo) -> returned. Recommend we send them instructions to re-submit with correct IBAN and offer to reimburse any bank fees if they can provide proof. We should also ask their bank for an indemnity claim?

lydia_bankops: For returned funds due to beneficiary account not found, the originator should get funds back automatically. If they want us to chase, we need an indemnity and proof of fees. We can also offer to accept a wire with intermediary bank details to speed it.

ana_support: Draft reply for approval: short apology, explain returned due to IBAN mismatch, ask them to re-send with corrected IBAN, request copy of their bank fees to reimburse, and offer to hold their account in good standing so no service disruption. 

jun_finance: Approve. Also add: if they need an alternate payment method (ACH/credit card), we can provide instructions and a one-time link.

tom_custliaison: Sending draft now. I'll attach our verified wire instructions and include that we'll reimburse proven sending-bank charges.

payments_bot: Internal action: set invoice INV-2026-0310 status -> investigation_inbound_return; tag: returned-invalid-iban; owner=jun_finance.

max_devops: Follow-up: I'll add an IBAN checksum validation ticket to the backlog (ENG-PI-1187) so the billing form flags obvious typos.

lydia_bankops: Closing loop: if customer re-sends and their bank can confirm the previous debit was returned, finance should mark original external_ref as returned_completed and reconcile once we receive funds/retry.

ana_support: Thanks all. Tom — keep this thread updated when the customer confirms re-send or provides fee receipts. :thumbsup:

tom_custliaison: Will do.
